title: Distinguish local list readiness from authoritative empty results

requirements.invariant: List presentation renders immutable read state and emits typed user intent while owning no authorization rule, persistence path, multi-record write, server commitment inference, or backend SDK value.
A list control selects a named query profile, sort, filter, search, page, retry, add, or selection intent; it never turns those values into a generic repository or an untyped domain write.

List state carries stable query/cursor and readiness metadata so authoritative empty, no local matches, incomplete subscription, partial data, stale data, and failure remain different representable outcomes.

Every query, sort, filter, cursor, failure, and intent value uses Ledger or standard Swift types; arbitrary field names, SQL, collection paths, dynamic dictionaries, SDK listener handles, and vendor errors cannot cross the boundary.

Deterministic reference fixtures prove cached-first rendering, readiness transitions, restart reconstruction, non-enumerating failure, retry intent, bounded query state, and stable ordering without a network or provider adapter.

items: NamedQueryProfileID, NamedSortID, NamedFilterID, StableCursor, and LocalDataVersion are validated stable values with no persistence-field or provider meaning.
StableSortDescriptor selects one reviewed named sort, direction, cursor contract version, and stable-entity-ID tie-breaker; the UI never submits a raw field name.
ListQueryState contains one named profile plus only validated sort, filter, normalized search, bounded page-size, and opaque cursor state.
ListReadiness, ListEmptyState, and ListFailureState form closed non-overlapping outcomes; unavailable/not-authorized/not-found presentation cannot enumerate inaccessible entity existence.
ListPresentationIntent is a closed typed set for query changes, retry, add, and selection; presentation cannot synthesize a business command.

postgresSchema.notApplicable: Shared presentation contracts introduce no target relation, view, function, index, or persistence schema.

serverHandlers.notApplicable: This slice executes no query or business command; owning feature slices later bind named profiles and intents to their ports.

dataApiGrants.notApplicable: No Data API schema or relation is exposed.

rlsPolicies.notApplicable: No server row/function is introduced; authorization remains the owning query projection's obligation.

syncStreams.notApplicable: The slice consumes abstract readiness metadata and defines no PowerSync Stream or row visibility.

items: A pure ListPresentationReducer accepts local query snapshots and metadata without waiting for network state, preserves the last locally usable snapshot through partial/stale transitions, and never converts incomplete data into authoritative empty.
Reconstructing the reducer from the same query state and local snapshot produces the same presentation state; transient retry emits a typed RetryQueryIntent without discarding cached rows.

Authorization/not-found failures collapse into one non-enumerating unavailable state, while retryable infrastructure failure remains explicit and cached rows stay visibly stale rather than disappearing.

storageMedia.notApplicable: No attachment identity, byte, object, or display-source contract is introduced.

appMcp.notApplicable: These are reusable app-presentation contracts only; MCP receives the owning named query contracts, not UI control state.

migrationReconciliation.notApplicable: Transient list state is not migrated and no Firebase record is read.

observabilityRunbooks.notApplicable: This slice emits no telemetry; later feature presenters may record bounded readiness categories without query contents.

items: The contracts and reference reducer are additive target-only Swift code, import no provider SDK, alter no current app project, contact no hosted service, and activate no production behavior.
Owning feature slices opt into the contracts individually; reverting this foundation before cutover removes only target-only code and tests.

verification.expected: Stable identifiers, named sorts/filters, bounded query state, opaque cursors, closed intents, deterministic tie metadata, and invalid-value rejection behave without raw fields or backend values.
The same locally available snapshot and query state reconstruct identical ready/partial/stale presentation after restart, and incomplete readiness never becomes authoritative empty.
Unavailable/not-found/authorization outcomes do not enumerate existence; retryable failure preserves visibly stale cached rows and emits a typed retry intent; invalid transitions fail closed.

verification.owner: pull-request CI Isolated target environment job
verification.expected: The exact implementation commit passes conversion traceability, source-contamination and generated-contract checks, all target tests, macOS and generic iOS Simulator target builds, and clean tracked-diff validation.

notes: Decision-independent shared presentation foundation derived from the app-shell capability dossier. It deliberately stops before concrete Item/Project/Invoice filters, UI snapshots, provider adapters, local database implementation, Auth, Sync Streams, product commands, hosted resources, migration, or production authority.
